name: Stage 42: Koppartorp to Skyrshyttan
description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 42, Koppartorp to Skyrshyttan.
utilities: Koppartorp is the strong service/access node with parking, Tunabergs kyrka bus stop, toilet, seasonal summer tap, Tunabergs hembygdsgård cafe/museum, Koppartorps rastplats, and mining heritage. The cafe/museum is summer-seasonal and should not be treated as year-round food.
Skyrshyttan is a sparse endpoint and stage 43 junction. Official stage 43 information says there is no good parking at the stage start, only possible roadside space for perhaps one car.

Skyrshyttan-side transit is usually via Munksäter/Munksätter bus stop plus roughly 15 minutes of walking. Knaptorp can be a useful mid-stage bus workaround if line 561 timing fits. Koppartorp/Tunabergs kyrka service may be limited, weekday-heavy, or demand-responsive; verify live Sörmlandstrafiken.
No shop, shelter, designated campsite, verified toilet, or potable water was found mid-stage or at Skyrshyttan.
waterSources: The only verified refill is the Koppartorp church/hembygd summer tap at the start. It is seasonal, not year-round.
No verified potable mid-stage water or Skyrshyttan water was found. Carry water before leaving Koppartorp; treat any natural water as unverified.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden lists stage 42 as 7 km, the 2025 long-distance pass lists 6.5 km, Naturkartan exposes about 6319 m, OSM relation 6575013 measures about 6.6 km, Äventyrligare 6.62 km, AllTrails 6.8 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 6.32 km. Use 7 km as the rounded official planning distance with a measured-line caveat.

Public metadata around stage 42 is inconsistent: OSM relation 6575013 has correct endpoints, stage tags and a 2025 update, while OSM-wiki/search snippets and external tables mix 6.3, 6.5, 7, or stale 10 km/0% values. Prefer Sörmlandsleden/Naturkartan/current local geometry for planning.

Main-route topology runs from Koppartorp/stage 41 to Skyrshyttan/stage 43. For route-builder stitching, snap to OSM node 2889617483 at 58.645025,16.900148 and OSM node 12765514559 at 58.676255,16.886758; local endpoints are close and the current local drawing is usable.
Koppartorp is also a hub for stage 37:2, Gruvslingan, Kummelbergsrundan, Simonberget options, and Tunabergsrundan context.

This is a culture-heavy mining and history stage through Tunaberg bergslag. Official route highlights include Tunabergs hembygdsgård, mine holes, Storgruvan, Kalkberget, Grishyttan, jättegrytor near Älvbro, viewpoints, ormgran/larch stand, Stora Jogershyttan, and old railway embankment toward Skyrshyttan.

Tunaberg-Koppartorp is a national-interest cultural environment for mining and works history, including cobalt, iron and copper mining, medieval smelting remains, and old road/industrial structures. Treat it as protected heritage context, not just scenery.

Old mining remains, mine holes, slag heaps, giant potholes, furnace sites, and old railway structures should be treated as look-but-do-not-disturb heritage and safety hazards. Storgruvan is reported as about 160 m deep and more than 400 m long; stay on marked paths and keep children/dogs close near mine holes.

No official reroute/fault report was found for stage 42 during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Place names appear stable: Koppartorp, Kalkberget, Grishyttan, Älvbro, Stora Jogershyttan/Stor-Jägershyttans gamla tomt, Skyrshyttan.

Team Vildmark, Nya Stigar, SPF and LoisansRundor reports support the stage-42/43 character: varied forest, paths, gravel roads, old crofts, mine areas, giant's kettles, old railway bed, wet grass in poor weather, and a useful Knaptorp bus access point. No credible stage-42-specific bad-marking report was found.

The stage is short but not entirely flat. User reports and AllTrails indicate small climbs, wet/high vegetation at times, knobbly terrain, roots/rock, and moderate ascent around Koppartorp-Kalkberget-Grishyttan and the mining landscape.

No shelter or designated campsite was found on stage 42. A stale user report mentioned an informal homemade rest shelter, likely for hunters; do not map it as official or dependable overnight infrastructure. Use allemansrätten only where appropriate and follow local signs; nearby Simonberget/Kummelberget reserve rules apply if combining with local loops.

The route may cross or edge cultivated/private land in places. Stay on marked trail/roads, do not spread out over fields/crops, avoid yards/private driveways, keep dogs close, and do not block forestry or farm access.

Fires should be limited to the prepared Koppartorp/Storgruvan rest area and only when current fire-ban rules allow it. Stricter bans can prohibit fixed grill places too, and fires should never be made on rock slabs or bedrock.

Kummelberget bird-protection closure and Simonberget tent/fire rules matter for nearby loop combinations: Kummelberget closed February 1-August 15; Simonberget tenting only between toilet and fireplace below the hill for max two nights.
